language.script_notes: Spanish appears more in Florida (especially south Florida) than elsewhere in the region; French/Cajun influence in Louisiana place names.

road_furniture.line_paint: Noticeably more unpaved/gravel rural roads than the Northeast.
road_furniture.curb_style: Open roadside ditches common in rural areas rather than curbs; kudzu vine often smothers roadside trees, poles and embankments — a very strong regional tell.

architecture.roof_style: Simple gable roofs on wood-frame houses; wide covered porches common on older Southern homes.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal roofing common on rural/older buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Wood-frame siding and red brick construction; raised/elevated houses common in flood-prone Gulf coast areas; shotgun houses in older Southern towns.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Red clay/brick tones dominate built material (the region's distinctive red-brick buildings come directly from the local red clay soil); white-painted wood siding also common.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Wide-porched Southern houses; shotgun houses; Spanish-moss-draped oak-lined avenues in the Deep South; Gulf coast beach houses on stilts; small-town courthouse squares.

nature.vegetation: Yellow/loblolly/longleaf pine forest on red clay soil is the single strongest regional tell; kudzu vine smothering trees and roadsides; Spanish moss hanging from live oaks in the Deep South and coastal areas; palmetto and subtropical vegetation in Florida.
nature.terrain: Gently rolling red-clay hills through Georgia/Alabama/the Carolinas (the 'Red Hills'), flattening into coastal plain toward the Gulf and Atlantic; flat and swampy in Louisiana/Florida.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid, green year-round; hazy summer light; hurricanes/heavy rain common in Gulf coast imagery.

vehicles.plate_color: Varies by state — Georgia peach-themed plate, Florida orange-with-citrus-leaf, Louisiana fleur-de-lis motifs, Texas varies by design year.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Pickup trucks especially common; more visible rust/older vehicle stock in poorer rural counties.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of generations; rural areas sometimes carry older/lower-quality imagery.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage in and around cities (Atlanta, Nashville, New Orleans, Miami); thinner in deep rural stretches.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Rural farmland, wood-frame houses, similar road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The South has red clay soil, pine forest, kudzu and Spanish moss with a hot humid green look year-round; the Midwest is flatter, more corn/soy cropland, and noticeably less humid-hazy in imagery.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Subtropical Gulf coast vegetation, humid climate, palm trees in Florida/coastal areas
confusion_set.tiebreaker: US plates, yellow center lines, and English signage vs. Mexican Spanish signage and different plate formats; Mexican road infrastructure and architecture differ noticeably even in similar climates.
